title: Senior AI Engineer / AI Systems Architect (Python, Multi-Agent Systems)
description:
Anyé Capital is an AI-driven quantitative trading and research company building proprietary algorithmic-trading infrastructure, advanced backtesting systems, and an internal workforce of specialized AI agents.



We are seeking a senior engineer to own the architecture and execution of Anyé Capital OS. This is not a basic chatbot or no-code automation role. You will turn an existing multi-agent platform—including agent registries, model integrations, tools, evaluation systems, and internal applications—into a reliable production system.



Responsibilities include designing multi-agent orchestration and task routing; building tool use, memory, retrieval, and persistent workflows; integrating model APIs and local models; developing Python backend services and APIs; implementing secure execution, permissions, approval gates, logging, and auditability; improving agent evaluation and failure recovery; establishing Git, testing, and engineering standards; and helping build an Agent Factory for creating and improving specialized AI employees.



Required qualifications: 5+ years of professional software engineering experience; advanced Python; demonstrated production work with tool-using LLM agents; backend architecture, REST APIs, databases, and asynchronous systems; Git, automated testing, debugging, and CI/CD; and strong written English. Experience with LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI, Claude Code, OpenAI or Anthropic APIs, MCP, RAG, Docker, PostgreSQL, or local-model infrastructure is valuable.



To apply, include your résumé, GitHub or portfolio, your most advanced agent system, how you tested it, and how you prevent an agent from falsely reporting success. Include your availability and expected monthly compensation. Shortlisted candidates may be offered a paid, synthetic technical assessment.

title: Quantitative Researcher / Algorithmic Trading Strategist — Futures
description:
Anyé Capital is seeking a quantitative researcher to develop and challenge systematic trading strategies, with emphasis on futures markets such as NQ, ES, and gold.



You will formulate testable hypotheses; evaluate breakout, EMA pullback, VWAP, mean-reversion, and related strategies; design statistically sound backtests; analyze market regimes, drawdowns, risk-adjusted returns, slippage, commissions, and execution constraints; identify overfitting, leakage, and lookahead bias; and produce clear research specifications for implementation by quantitative developers.



Required qualifications include Python, pandas, NumPy, statistical analysis, time-series research, backtesting, futures-market knowledge, and the ability to explain statistical significance, walk-forward testing, realistic fills, and out-of-sample validation. Experience with NinjaTrader, TradingView, portfolio construction, market microstructure, or institutional systematic trading is preferred.



This role is for a rigorous researcher, not a discretionary signal seller. You must be willing to conclude that a strategy has no proven edge when the evidence does not support it.



To apply, include a résumé or portfolio, a sanitized example of a strategy research project, your validation methodology, the most common ways backtests mislead researchers, your availability, and expected monthly compensation. Shortlisted candidates may receive a paid assessment using synthetic data and an intentionally flawed backtest.

title: Python Quant Developer / Backtesting Engineer
description:

Experience with futures data, C#, NinjaScript, NinjaTrader, event-driven systems, or performance optimization is preferred.

title: Media Buyer/Paid Ads Specialist
description:
Company Info

The Scale Space is a marketing agency that runs full-funnel growth for clients: paid ads, automation, and strategy. Small, fast-moving team based in North Hollywood, CA, operating fully remote. The promise to clients is revenue, not traffic, clicks, or vanity metrics.



Compensation & Logistics

- Base salary: $1200-$2000, based on experience

- Opportunity for performance based bonuses (not guaranteed), tied to the results you drive on your accounts

- Fully remote, work from home, permanently

- Full-time, 8 hours/day with breaks, PST/PDT

- Working hours: 9am to 5pm PST

- Benefits: 15 vacation, 8 sick, 2 personal, 4 bereavement, 6 holidays, 25 maternity/paternity company-paid days

- Sole full-time commitment



Mission

Own paid media for our client book end to end. Build and run the campaigns, write the ads, own the tracking underneath them, and turn the performance data into decisions the team and the client can act on. When a client asks why cost per lead moved, you are the person who already knows and already has the fix in motion.



What This Role Actually Is

Anyone can tell a client that cost per lead went up. We need someone who can say why it went up, what it is costing the client in real revenue, and the specific change that fixes it. That is the whole job.

You will run roughly 8 to 10 brands across med spa, hospitality, real estate, and home services. Meta is our primary platform, Google is growing, and a couple of accounts run wider than that. You will sit in on client meetings alongside the CEO and the Customer Success Manager, and you will be the one answering the technical questions when they come.



Key Responsibilities

1. Run the ads

- Build, launch, and manage campaigns across Meta Ads and Google Ads

- Own audiences, offers, creative testing, budget pacing, learning phases, fatigue, and wasted spend

- Make the call on what to scale, what to kill, and what to test next, without asking permission for every budget change

- Monitor new launches closely through the first 72 hours

2. Write the ads

- Write ad copy, hooks, and angles for the campaigns you run

- Test copy the way you test everything else: against the number, not against opinion

- Feed the creative team what the data is telling you. Which hooks are holding attention, which formats are fatiguing, what the next round of creative needs to test. You are not writing the creative brief or art directing it, our creative lead and designers own that, but they need your read on performance to make good calls.

3. Own the tracking

- Set up and maintain pixel and CAPI, conversion events, and UTM structure across accounts

- Debug attribution when platform numbers and CRM numbers disagree, and they will disagree

- Connect ad platforms to client CRMs (GoHighLevel / Scale CRM and HubSpot) so spend ties back to booked revenue

- Know the difference between a platform-reported conversion and money in the client's bank account, and care about closing that gap

4. Report and recommend

- Own weekly and monthly performance reporting across your accounts

- Pull from the ad platforms and the CRM, and build the picture of where money is being made and lost

- Every report ends in a recommendation. A report without a "here is what we should do" is half finished.

- Use the 1-3-1: one problem, three possible solutions, one recommendation

5. Face the client

- Join client calls and speak to performance directly: what the numbers say, what changed, what you are doing about it

- Translate media buying into plain language for owners who do not think in ROAS

- Hold your position when the numbers support it, and say so plainly when a client's request will hurt their results

6. Self-QA

- Check your own work. Campaigns are set up correctly before they spend a dollar, and the numbers in a report are right before anyone sees them.

- Catch problems before the client does, fix them, then report what you fixed

-Document how your accounts and reporting work so nothing lives only in your head



Desired Experience & Requirements

- 2+ years managing multiple ad accounts at the same time. Agency side preferred. Running one in-house brand is not the same job.

- Meta Ads: deep, hands-on. You know the platform cold, not just the theory.

- Google Ads: real working knowledge across Search and Performance Max. Strong Meta with solid Google is fine.

- Tracking and attribution: you have set up pixel and CAPI yourself, and you have debugged a tracking problem rather than escalating it.

- Ad copywriting: you write your own ads and you can show us ones that worked.

- Data: comfortable in spreadsheets, able to structure messy data, able to find the story in the numbers. Looker Studio, Supermetrics, or similar is a plus.

- CRM: you can get into a CRM, find the lead and revenue data, and tie it to the ads. GoHighLevel and HubSpot are a plus; one CRM known well means you will learn ours.

- Client-facing: you can hold a performance conversation with a business owner without hiding behind jargon.

- AI-native: you use AI tools daily to move faster, and you know the difference between using AI and passing raw AI output off as your recommendation.

- Sole full-time commitment.



Tools You'll Work In

Meta Ads Manager, Google Ads, GoHighLevel / Scale CRM, HubSpot, SegMetrics, Google Sheets, Looker Studio, Claude, Slack, Notion, Loom. We will teach you the ones you do not know if the core skills are there.



What Success Looks Like

1. First 30 days

Audited every ad account and its tracking setup, and flagged what is broken

Took over reporting for your accounts and shipped it on schedule without being chased

Named the top three opportunities and the top three leaks across the book

2. First 60 days

Running optimization independently, with recommendations the team acts on

Writing your own ad copy across accounts

Caught and fixed account or tracking issues before they reached a client

Speaking to your numbers on client calls

3. First 90 days

Owning paid media, copy, tracking, and reporting for the full book with light oversight

Shipped changes that moved real client numbers, and can prove which changes did it

The person everyone asks when they want to know where the money is going



KPIs

Cost per acquisition and qualified lead rate by account; return on ad spend; reporting delivered on time with a recommendation attached; tracking accuracy between platform and CRM; client retention on accounts you run.



Who This Is Not For

- People who can launch campaigns but cannot read the data behind them

- People who send reports without a recommendation attached

- People who need permission for every budget change

- People who escalate a tracking problem instead of solving it

- People who paste AI output through as their own thinking

- People who go quiet when something breaks

- People looking for a quiet remote job to coast in



Core Values (culture fit screen)

- Speed Is King. Momentum over sitting tasks, progress before perfection.

- Extreme Ownership. Treat the business like your own, fill gaps, bring ideas.

- Results Over Excuses. Half done is not done. Output quality over effort.

- Never Stop Growing. Noticeably better every 90 days.

- Clear and Direct Communication. Speak up early, bring solutions with problems.



What We Offer

Base salary with the opportunity for performance based bonuses. Bonuses are not guaranteed. They are earned on the results you drive, because we would rather reward someone for moving real numbers than pay a flat rate for activity.

This is a long-term seat, not a gig. You own paid media for the whole company, and as we grow the function grows under you. We promote from the inside when someone earns it.

Fully remote, permanently. We measure results, not hours logged.



How to Apply

1. Send us your portfolio

2. Tell us about a time the data changed how you were running an account. What did the numbers say, what did you change, and what happened after? Be specific. Bring real examples of campaigns you have run, ad copy you have written, and reporting you have built.





We read every application that shows us how you think. Generic applications do not make it past the first read.

title: Executive Assistant-Right Hand-Fast-Growing Comic Book Company
description:
Operations Manager-Execution Partner-Project Killer-Fast-Growing Comic Book Company

Own the operations backbone of a niche comic book brand, work directly with leadership, and get promoted fairly by numbers.



This role is for that special person who wants to become truly exceptional. If that’s you, you already know this message is your signal.



What You Get If You Win Here

- High autonomy: once you’re ramped, you own your queue, schedule, and methods as long as the KPIs are hit. Lots of freedom to figure it out, great for someone that loves building with Legos

- Direct proximity to leadership: you work daily with the Ops Manager on the most important projects in the company.

- Clear advancement path: your growth is tied to visible numbers (tasks shipped, zero-miss cadence, freed founder/ops time, profit/leading metrics), not politics.

- Insane skill growth: the pace and standards here mean every 12 months with us will feel like 3 years of experience in a normal VA/ops role. You can leapfrog your friends. If you join this will change your life. You will work harder than you’ve ever worked before and grow faster than you’ve ever grown before.

- Comic Books!: you’re not just pushing random SaaS tickets; you’re inside a real comic book store seeing rare old comic books, private deals, and the business behind the Hollywood Marvel Movies that everyone loves!

If you’re that person who enjoys working really hard to the point that it takes 2-3 people to do what you did listen up:

Our tasks in asana for projects and ongoing operations are moving at a snail’s pace.

Ops Manager + CEO is chasing tasks, slack policing, cleaning up Asana, and re-explaining context instead of focusing on their jobs.



We’ve had “pleasant” VAs who:

Can’t drive tasks to completion independently

Mark tasks complete with no proof

Miss reports/skip cadence and require chasing.

Drift on ownership, urgency & follow thru

Need hand-holding

I don’t need another task hopper. I need a project killer who comes into ambiguity, creates structure, drives tasks to completion, and actually frees the Ops Manager to focus on his key projects. If this works, his deep work hours and project output go up because you’re handling everything else. We will measure that and tie your promotions/raises to it. This is not for everyone. We’re looking for winners.



What You’ll Actually Do

You will be Ops Manager’s execution partner and force-multiplier. Concrete outputs:

Own Asana: every task has an owner, due date, Done Check, and proof link when completed

Maintain an active queue of 20+ meaningful tasks, prioritized against our key rocks (Marketing, Sales, Ongoing Operations, Cleanup, Admin)

Ship 25+ tasks/week with proof, minimal rework, and zero “ghosted” items

Proactively handle operational issues/fires in designated lanes

Maintain Reporting at Set Cadence, Follow-up loops across projects

Add leverage: plug AI into our workflows (Asana, docs, reports) to make us faster and cleaner without being asked

We do NOT need more SOPS-although you might tighten them on the fly. We need someone to do the operations. If you want to sit and write playbooks all day, this is the wrong seat-that will be an earned responsibility later. If you aren’t ready to work hard daily do not apply.



How We Set You Up To Win (First 90 Days)

We don’t just throw you in the deep end. In your first 30 days, you’ll shadow the Ops Manager, learn our Asana + reporting systems, and get a clear scorecard so you always know what “great” looks like. By 30 days, you’ll own your own project lanes with weekly 1:1s for feedback, support, and removing blockers so you can move faster instead of guessing what we want.



Real Growth Example

One of our Filipino teammates started with us on basic execution work at ~$800/month. Over time, he took ownership of his queue, fixed broken processes, and became the person we trusted to “just handle it.” As his scope grew, so did his comp and stability. Now he makes ~$2,500/month (and we’re working on getting him even more) because he stuck with it and actually grew. A lot of people say they want that, but their resumes show 6–12 month hops. The pattern here is simple: prove you can own outcomes over time, and we grow your responsibilities, trust, and pay accordingly.



Schedule, Hours & Time Zone (No Surprises)

This is a full time, US hours role (roughly US Eastern business hours) with a true 50–60 hour workweek during this growth season. Expect most weeks to be closer to that 60 hour mark. If you want a strict 40 hour cap, this is the wrong seat; if you want a place where extra effort is noticed, measured, and rewarded, you’ll feel at home here. This is not just a job. This is a commitment.



What Winning Looks Like

By Day 30: Ops Manager is spending ~95% of his time on projects, not Slack/Asana/admin fires, because you’re handling those and executing projects alongside him. Profit and leading metrics are moving up faster because of you



By 12 months: You are Ops Manager’s go to operator & on track to become Ops Manager. Nothing important moves in Ops without you knowing. You own the Asana board, key ops projects, and reporting cadence. You’re the person we trust to “just handle it,” and your comp reflects that increased ownership.



If you become that go to operator, you’ll have real say in how we run Ops – you won’t just be ‘executing tickets,’ you’ll help design the system.”



Who This Is NOT For

You prefer to ‘coordinate’ and assign tasks to others instead of doing the work yourself with excellence.

You want to manage people before you’ve truly proven you can personally execute at a high level.

You want a chill, low-pressure 9–5

You need to be told what to do all day and hate being judged by objective numbers

You mark tasks complete without proof or next steps

You change jobs every 6–18 months and blame the company/manager/market/

You get defensive or freeze when given direct feedback or pressure

You are currently juggling multiple full time clients and want to “squeeze us in” on the side.

You are mass applying to dozens of jobs and just want to see who bites first.





Who This IS For

You’ve stayed 2–3+ years in at least one role and can prove outcomes

You like pressure, highly competitive environments, being the one who “gets it done” when others stall

You’ve built systems (trackers, automations, SOPs), not just followed them

You are tech-comfortable: Asana (or similar), CRMs, zaps, AI tools, simple web/ops/marketing stacks

You’re willing to bet on one company instead of juggling lots of smaller, easier gigs.

You hate corporate BS– endless meetings, vague goals, and politics – and would rather be rewarded for what you actually create.

You’re happy to grind 50–60 hours/week no issues. We’re in a BIG growth & push season. It will be like this for the next year and then we’ll see. Everyone wants to grow a lot, but it’s actually happening here.



Comp & Growth

(All of this is written into your contract.)

Months 1–3: Ramp / Trial

• $800/month base, guaranteed, while you learn our systems and we test fit.

• No bonus in this phase. You’re paid to prove you can hit the KPI floors.

Month 4+ – Performance Based Upside

• Base stays at $800 until you’ve hit KPI floors for 2 straight months. After that, base increases to $900/month going forward.

• On top of base, you can earn:

$400 bonus in months where you hit 3 out of 4 KPIs (with Output as one of them).

$1,000 bonus in months where you hit 4 out of 4 KPIs on the weekly scorecard.

• In practice, that means:

Solid performance months ~$1,200–$1,300/month

Killer months (4/4 KPIs)~$1,800–$1,900/month

All bonuses are 100% KPI based (shipped outcomes, taking load off the Ops Manager, zero CEO/manager rescues, tight open loops) and 4/5 culture.



Training & Growth Investment (on top of pay)

We actively invest in making you a sharper teammate. Over time, we’ll put thousands of dollars into your development (courses, coaching, playbooks, and tools) that we choose together based on what will make you more effective in this seat.

We also protect uninterrupted deep work blocks for you every week (no rando ---------- etings, no Slack spam). You’re paid to ship outcomes, not sit in back to back Zoom calls.



Important: This is an ON FIELD role. You will not have a team under you to delegate to.

95% of your time is doing the work yourself, 5% is light coordination. If your default mode is to make plans and pass tasks to others, this will be a bad fit.



Compensation here is performance based. Raises are earned through clearly exceeding KPIs and demonstrating core values consistently. If you want “stability” to mean “I can coast and still get raises,” this won’t feel stable. If you want stability to mean “the better I get, the more valuable and secure I become,” you’ll like it here.



How To Apply (24-Hour Test)

Our Hiring Process (So There Are No Surprises)

If your 24 hour answers impress us, the next steps are:

A short interview focused on your past execution.

A live 60 minute work trial inside our real tools where you’ll work directly with the Ops Manager. We do this because talk is cheap. If you don’t like being tested on real work before getting hired, this won’t be a fit.



Do NOT click quick-apply. In the next 24 hours, you must:

Reply with answers to ALL of these (short but specific; bullets are fine):

Q1: Describe the most complex project you personally drove fro ---------- ssy start to completion where you did most of the execution yourself, not just assigning tasks. Include at least one example of how you set your own deadlines and moved forward when other people were slow to respond.”

Q2: Share 3 links or screenshots (Google Docs, Sheets, Asana boards, trackers, automations, etc.) that you built yourself which show how you organize and drive work. Briefly explain each.

Q3: You have 30 tasks due this week and realize you’ll miss 5. Walk me through, step-by-step, how you handle it with your manager and stakeholders.

Q4: Below are 6 messy “tasks” we actually see (all dumped into one list):

– “Fix Asana, it’s a mess”

– “Seller lead texting follow up??”

– “Finance com/projections cadence d2 ”

– “Inventory backlog insane”

– “Need better reporting”

– “Update SOPs

In this role you will NOT have anyone to delegate to assume it’s just you and the Ops Manager.



1. In a Google Doc, please:



Rewrite these into clear tasks with: Owner (you or Ops Manager), Due Date (next 7–30 days), and a concrete Done Check + proof required. “Write your task descriptions as if you are committing: ‘I will do X by Y time. If Z doesn’t happen by [time], here’s my fallback.’ Generic ‘follow up / request access’ answers will fail you.”



2. Put them in the order you’d actually do them and explain why in 3–5 bullet points.



3. Link the Google Doc here (view access).

Spend no more than 30–45 minutes. If you can’t figure this out on your own, this role will be too hard in real life – that’s okay, just skip applying.



Attach your PDF resume/Google Drive link.

title: Property Manager / Operations Manager / Project Manager for Property Management Company

We need a resourceful, organized operator to take ownership of day-to-day operations: someone who thinks a step ahead, closes the loop, and makes sure work moves from "reported" to "done" without being chased.

If you're sharp, organized, and a fast learner, we'll teach you our systems. **Growth-Minded & Solutions-Focused:** We don't dwell on problems; we find solutions. We want people who are hungry to learn, grow, and improve our systems every day.

**A Relationship, Not a Transaction:** We want a years-long partnership where you feel supported, trusted, and empowered to make decisions.



**Impact Over Activity:** We value outcomes. You won't be micromanaged; you will be given clear goals and the freedom to execute, along with the support to be able to succeed.

title: Case Manager - Lemon Law
description:
Summary

**Remote | California Lemon Law Firm | Full-Time

 

** We are a California law firm focused on lemon law and consumer protection litigation, and we are looking for a licensed attorney to join our team as a Case Manager. 

 

This is a hands-on position for an attorney who can manage cases, communicate directly with clients, stay on top of deadlines, and move cases forward from intake through settlement. 

 

## What You’ll Do 

* Manage an assigned caseload from intake/retainer through settlement or resolution. 

* Communicate directly with clients, provide case updates, answer routine questions, and maintain strong client relationships. 

* Request, review, and organize documents and evidence from clients. 

* Review purchase documents, repair orders, warranty records, service history, manufacturer communications, and other case-related documents. 

* Analyze case facts and identify missing information, potential issues, and case strengths/weaknesses. 

* Draft legal documents, including pleadings, discovery, meet-and-confer correspondence, declarations, motions, settlement documents, and other case-related correspondence. 

* Prepare and file documents with the court and assist with e-filing as needed. 

* Track case deadlines, hearings, discovery obligations, settlement deadlines, and other important dates. 

* Coordinate with attorneys, paralegals, case managers, and other members of the team. 

* Maintain accurate and organized case files and case-management records. 

* Follow cases closely and make sure nothing falls through the cracks. 

* Escalate significant legal or case issues when attorney review or strategy decisions are needed. 

 

## What We’re Looking For **Required:** 

 

* An active attorney license in good standing. 

* Experience handling lemon law cases OR civil litigation. 

* Strong legal writing and analytical skills. 

* Excellent communication and client-management skills. 

* Ability to independently manage multiple cases and competing deadlines. 

* Strong organizational skills and attention to detail. 

* Ability to work independently in a remote environment. 

* Professional, responsive, and comfortable communicating directly with clients. 

 

## Preferred 

* Direct California lemon law experience. 

* Experience handling cases from intake through settlement. 

* Experience with pleadings, discovery, motions, settlement negotiations, and court filings. 

* Experience using case-management software such as Filevine. 

* Experience working in a remote law-firm environment. 

 

## The Ideal Candidate 

We are looking for someone who can own their cases rather than simply complete individual assignments. You should be comfortable communicating with clients, reviewing documents, drafting legal work, managing deadlines, coordinating with the team, and keeping a case moving without needing to be reminded about every next step. If you have lemon law experience, that's a strong advantage. If you have solid civil litigation experience and can learn the firm's lemon law process, we are also interested in speaking with you. 

 

## How to Apply 

 

Please submit your resume and a brief introduction explaining your relevant lemon law or civil litigation experience. 

 

### Important 

Read Before Applying To confirm that you have read the entire job posting, include the title and author of the latest book you've read in the subject line of your application. Applications that do not include the code word may not be considered.

title: Supply Chain Operations Associate
description:

We’re a fast-growing beauty brand creating “ready-to-wear” makeup.

Our viral product is a press-on eyeshadow that applies in 5 seconds (press • peel • done). We’ve been featured in Cosmopolitan, Marie Claire, and the TODAY Show, and our content has generated millions of organic views across TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube. 

We’re growing fast, and are launching new products, so our supply chain is about to get a lot more interesting.

We’re looking for a part-time Operations Associate to own our supply chain day to day (starting at 2-3 hours per week, ramping up to 10 hours per week, then an opportunity to join full-time). If stockouts keep you up at night and a clean inventory sheet makes you happy, keep reading.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

Purchasing & supplier management

Place and track purchase orders with multiple suppliers

Follow up on production timelines, confirm ship dates, and flag delays early

Track inbound shipments from supplier to warehouse

Keep supplier communication organized and professional

Inventory & demand planning

Keep 100+ SKUs in stock and prevent stockouts

Manage and update our demand planning model to forecast what to reorder and when

Use our internal inventory planning software to have a weekly pulse on on-hand inventory

Flag low-stock risks before they become problems

Warehouse & fulfillment coordination

Coordinate daily with our 3PL warehouse to get orders out the door

Build a daily prioritized list of orders to ship (by urgency, event dates, and stock availability)

Create entries in our system for incoming POs

Set up new products and SKUs in our system ahead of launches

Cross-functional communication

Tell our customer service rep about out-of-stock and backorder situations so customers get accurate information

Support new product launches with inventory and timeline planning

Escalate unusual supply chain decisions to the founder with a clear recommendation, not just a problem

REQUIREMENTS (non-negotiable)

3+ years of supply chain / operations experience

Experience managing physical inventory at a DTC consumer products (CPG) company

Strong written English

Highly organized, with strong attention to detail

Comfortable with spreadsheets and learning new software

Reliable and responsive, with strong ownership

Able to follow a system and spot when the system needs to change

BONUS IF YOU HAVE

Experience with non-turnkey products (products where you source components or manage custom manufacturing, not just buy finished goods)

Experience with Shopify and 3PL systems

Experience with demand forecasting or inventory planning tools

Experience with beauty, cosmetics, or consumer goods

HOURS

Part-time: approximately 2-3 hours/week, ramping up to 10 hours/week, then opportunities to join full-time

Overlap with US Eastern Time hours required, specifically 9am–4pm ET (we coordinate with our warehouse in real time)

Long-term role with room to grow as the company grows

TO APPLY, PLEASE INCLUDE:

Send an
 to: 

A short introduction and your resume

A brief description of your DTC/CPG inventory experience: what you managed, how many SKUs, and which tools you used

One example of a stockout or supply chain problem you caught or solved, and what you did

Your rate and availability (including overlap with US Eastern hours)

The word “mothership” somewhere in your application so we know you read this entire posting



Thanks so much for your time and looking forward to meeting you!!

xx

Jenny, founder/CEO

title: Experienced U.S. Real Estate Bookkeeper | Rentals + Fix & Flips
description:
We are a small but growing U.S.-based real estate investment company seeking an experienced real estate bookkeeper to take ownership of our bookkeeping.



We currently operate two real estate businesses: one primarily holding furnished/mid-term rental properties and another focused on fix-and-flip properties.



We have not completed our bookkeeping for 2026 yet, so the first project will be setting up our books correctly, bringing everything current for the year, and then maintaining them monthly going forward.



We have an REI Hub account and would prefer to continue using it. Prior REI Hub experience is a strong plus, but we are open to an experienced real estate bookkeeper who is willing to learn the software.



We are looking for someone with experience in real estate transactions who can work independently. We want to provide access to our accounts, closing statements, receipts, invoices, loan documents and other records and have you maintain accurate books, asking us questions when something is unclear. It may be a bit disorganized in the the beginning before we had separate business banking accounts, but we are willing to learn how to best work with you to provide what you need to do the job!



The initial setup and 2026 catch-up may require additional time, and we anticipate allowing up to 20 hours to get everything organized and current. Once the initial setup is complete, we expect the ongoing workload to average approximately 2–3 hours per week. We’re looking for someone interested in continuing with us long-term as our real estate business grows.



Responsibilities include:

- Initial setup and 2026 catch-up bookkeeping

- Bank and credit-card reconciliation

- Categorizing transactions and matching receipts/invoices

- Tracking expenses by LLC and individual property

- Rental-property accounting

- Fix-and-flip/project accounting and job costing

- Recording property purchases and sales from closing statements

- Correctly recording mortgages, private/hard-money loans, principal, interest and other financing transactions

- Tracking rehab/construction expenses

- Owner contributions, distributions and transfers

- Monthly P&L and balance-sheet reporting

- Maintaining clean records for year-end handoff to our U.S. CPA



Ideal candidate:



- 3+ years bookkeeping/accounting experience preferred

- Significant experience with U.S. real estate investors

- Experience with BOTH rental properties and fix-and-flips

- Comfortable with multiple LLCs/properties

- Experience reading U.S. closing statements

- Strong understanding of real-estate loans and property/project accounting

- Able to work independently and ask questions rather than guess

- Excellent written English and communication



This is a small portfolio, so we anticipate approximately 5–10 hours per month after the initial catch-up/setup project.



When applying, please tell us:



1. How many years have you done bookkeeping for U.S. real estate investors?

2. What experience do you have specifically with fix-and-flips?

3. Have you handled both rental and flip accounting for the same client?

4. Are you comfortable setting up books from scratch and catching up approximately 9 months of transactions?

6. What accounting/bookkeeping certifications or degrees do you have?

7. What is your hourly rate?

8. Please describe your current availability and approximately how many hours per month you are looking for.



We are specifically looking for an experienced bookkeeper/accounting professional who can take responsibility for maintaining accurate real-estate books.

title: Scientific Content Editor
description:
About Us:

At MSE Supplies, we power scientific breakthroughs. As a fast-growing supplier of advanced materials, lab equipment, and analytical instruments, we serve innovators in more than 70 countries—helping researchers, engineers, and manufacturers solve tough problems every day.



We’re on a mission to make top-tier scientific tools more accessible, more responsive, and more personal. That starts with providing clear, accurate, and deeply reliable technical knowledge to the global scientific community.



Position Overview:

MSE Supplies LLC is seeking a detail-oriented Scientific Content Editor with a strong STEM background to oversee our technical blog production pipeline. In this role, you will take drafts generated by our AI workflows and custom internal AI tools, then transform them into polished, rigorously fact-checked, and engaging technical articles that resonate with researchers, lab managers, and materials engineers.



You will collaborate closely with our dedicated SEO Specialist—taking their keyword roadmaps and content briefs and bringing them to life with high editorial standards, scientific accuracy, and natural tone. While we build the internal AI tooling and supply the SEO roadmap, you will be the editorial pilot overseeing the process: validating scientific claims, humanizing the prose, and maintaining our content pipeline.



Responsibilities:

⚬ Fact-Check & Validate Scientific Content: Rigorously review AI-generated drafts for scientific accuracy, proper chemical/materials terminology, methodology context, and valid data interpretation.

⚬ Humanize & Polish Drafts: Rewrite and edit content generated by our internal AI tools to eliminate robotic phrasing, improve narrative flow, add authentic lab context, and ensure a credible, authoritative brand voice.

⚬ Oversee Content Operations: Manage the end-to-end editorial pipeline—from running topics through our internal AI generators to final publication—ensuring a consistent cadence and exceptional output quality.

⚬ Light Content Strategy & Ideation: Partner with our SEO Specialist to translate keyword clusters into practical article outlines, educational guides, and product-adjacent topic ideas.

⚬ Process Feedback & Refinement: Provide operational feedback on outputs from our proprietary AI tools to help our technical team refine generation quality over time.

⚬ Product Catalog Integration: Naturally integrate MSE Supplies’ product categories (e.g., advanced ceramics, single crystals, battery materials, and lab equipment) into educational content without sounding overly promotional.

Qualifications and Skills:

⚬ Scientific Background: Degree or professional background in Materials Science, Chemistry, Physics, Chemical Engineering, or a closely related STEM field. Must be able to read and accurately interpret academic literature.

⚬ Editorial & Copywriting Excellence: Native-level English writing and editing skills with a sharp ear for voice, tone, and readability. Proven ability to translate complex lab concepts into clear, engaging prose.

⚬ Working AI Literacy: Comfortable using LLMs, AI writing interfaces, and internal automated content systems to oversee and guide production efficiently.

⚬ Editorial Pipeline Management: Experience managing a content calendar, technical blog pipeline, or scientific publication workflow.

⚬ Working SEO Literacy: Familiarity with on-page SEO basics (headers, internal linking, search intent) to execute direction provided by our SEO Specialist.

⚬ Self-Starter: Highly organized, proactive, and comfortable collaborating in a fast-paced, remote environment aligned with US business hours.



What Sets You Apart:

⚬ Prior experience writing, editing, or peer-reviewing for scientific B2B brands, academic journals, or technical trade publications.

⚬ Familiarity with on-page SEO tools such as SEMrush, Ahrefs, or Google Search Console.

⚬ Direct experience testing or providing feedback on internal AI generation workflows or custom LLM tooling.

title: Amazon FBA Product Research & Sourcing Specialist (Online Arbitrage + Wholesale)
description:
ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY



Laurielle Ventures is a growing Amazon FBA business, and we're looking for an experienced specialist to help us find the right products to sell through online arbitrage and wholesale.



The job is to find opportunities, check them carefully, and explain clearly whether we should pursue them. We value good judgment more than volume. A well-reasoned "no" is as useful to us as a strong "yes."



You need to already know Amazon sourcing well, because we need someone who can contribute from the start without introductory training.





WHAT YOU'LL DO



Product research and sourcing (main focus):

- Find and evaluate online arbitrage and wholesale product opportunities

- Research retailers, brands, distributors, and potential wholesale suppliers

- Review supplier price lists and pick out the promising wholesale opportunities

- Analyze demand, sales rank history, pricing history, competition, seasonality, and whether Amazon sells on the listing

- Calculate estimated net profit, ROI, and margins using purchase costs, Amazon fees, fulfillment costs, and other applicable expenses

- Before recommending a product, check selling eligibility, restrictions, possible intellectual property concerns, and other sourcing risks

- Present organized sourcing leads for our review, with supporting links, costs, calculations, and a clear recommendation



Operations support (secondary):

- Help with relevant Seller Central tasks

- Monitor inventory, stock levels, and replenishment needs

- Help with profitability calculations



Across all your work:

- Keep accurate, organized research records

- Tell us about progress, questions, and blockers without waiting to be asked



The owners make all purchasing decisions. Your role is to research and recommend.





REQUIRED EXPERIENCE



You must have:

- Proven hands-on experience researching and sourcing products for Amazon FBA through online arbitrage

- Proven experience researching wholesale suppliers and evaluating wholesale product opportunities

- Hands-on experience working in Amazon Seller Central

- Experience managing or monitoring Amazon inventory

- Experience using Amazon product research and sourcing tools

- Clear written English



Nice to have:

- Experience in the U.S. Amazon marketplace. Candidates with relevant experience in other Amazon marketplaces are also welcome.

- Familiarity with Aura, Claude, and/or 





TOOLS AND PREFERRED SKILLS



We give you the tools you need. We pay for all the software you need for this role, so you don't need to own or pay for any subscriptions. We already use several tools, and if there's one you recommend, prefer, or are more comfortable with, tell us. We'll review it, and once it's approved, we'll provide it. We want you to have everything you need to do your best work.



Tell us which of these tools (or others) you've actually used and how you used them. You don't need experience with all of them:

- Keepa

- SellerAmp SAS

- RevSeller

- IP Alert

- Seller 365

- Overlook Pro

- Other Amazon research, sourcing, profitability, or inventory tools



The person who does well here has:

- Strong research and analytical judgment

- Accuracy with numbers and attention to detail

- Initiative and the ability to work independently

- Reliable communication and follow-through

- Organized documentation habits

- The ability to explain why an opportunity is worth pursuing, and to recognize when a product should be rejected





HOURS, COMPENSATION, AND GROWTH



- Remote, part-time: 15–20 hours per week to start

- Flexible working hours

- Pay is flexible and depends on your experience and qualifications. Please tell us your expected hourly rate in USD.

- All required tools and software are provided



Most of your time will go to research and sourcing, not to a long list of unrelated tasks. You'll be contributing directly to a growing Amazon business. As we grow, you may be able to take on more hours and responsibility, including a possible move to full-time, depending on performance and business needs.





HOW TO APPLY



To be considered, you must complete both steps below:



Step 1: Submit your application directly through OnlineJobs.ph.



Step 2: Complete our Candidate Intake Form:





Applications will only be considered once both steps are completed. The intake form is a required part of your application, but it does not replace your OnlineJobs.ph application.



Please make sure your application includes:



1. Your résumé or a brief summary of your relevant Amazon experience, including the marketplaces you've worked in.

2. A short explanation of your online arbitrage and wholesale sourcing experience, including what you were personally responsible for.

3. The tools you've used and how you used them.

4. One brief example of a product opportunity you evaluated, covering your research, your profitability calculation, and your final recommendation.

   - A previously completed example is fine.

   - Please anonymize it and leave out any confidential client information.

   - We are not asking for new sourcing work as part of your application.

5. Your expected hourly rate in USD, your availability for 15–20 hours per week, and your earliest start date.



Short, specific answers are more useful to us than long ones.

Miami The Jeweler is hiring a skilled short-form video editor who wants consistent work, takes ownership, and is looking to grow with a brand long term.



We specialize in moissanite and diamond jewelry. We need someone who can turn raw footage into engaging Instagram Reels and TikToks that grab attention, keep people watching, and support sales.



We value three things: great edits, fast turnaround, and the ability to learn quickly.

Who We’re Looking For



- Strong editing instincts. You understand hooks, pacing, storytelling, captions, sound design, and when to keep an edit simple.

- Speed with quality.** You work efficiently, meet deadlines, and submit polished work.

- Fast learner. You apply feedback to future videos. The same corrections shouldn’t need to be repeated.

- Ownership. You check spelling, caption timing, audio levels, framing, and exports before submitting.

- Good judgment. You can follow a reference, make creative decisions independently, and ask clear questions when something is missing.

- Reliable communication. You’re responsive during agreed working hours and flag delays early.

- Drive to improve. You study content, bring ideas, and use performance feedback to improve your edits.





Responsibilities



- Edit Instagram Reels and TikToks from raw footage.

- Build strong opening hooks and clear, engaging stories.

- Use captions, cuts, effects, and audio intentionally to support the content.

- Adapt relevant trends and formats to our brand.

- Handle revisions promptly and keep track of brand preferences.

- Organize project files and deliver finished videos on schedule.

- Collaborate with our team to continuously improve content quality and performance.





Requirements



- A strong portfolio of short-form edits.

- Proficiency in Adobe Premiere Pro and CapCut—both required.

- Strong English comprehension and clear communication.

- Reliable computer, fast internet, and a smartphone for reviewing final edits.

- Availability for an exclusive, full-time commitment.





Pay, Availability & Long-Term Commitment



- Full-time monthly retainer.** Compensation will be discussed based on your skills, experience, and availability. Include your desired monthly rate when applying.

- Fast turnaround.** We expect prompt delivery, clear communication about delivery times, and polished edits with minimal back-and-forth as you learn our style.

- Evening availability required.** You must be available starting at **9 p.m. Eastern Time** and for an agreed working window afterward to collaborate, receive feedback, and handle edits. Include how late you’re available in Eastern Time when applying.

We regularly work with large 4K, 10-bit video files, so your setup must support an efficient, reliable editing workflow from day one.



- Powerful editing computer. You need a capable processor, sufficient RAM, graphics performance, and fast SSD storage to handle demanding footage without frequent freezing or excessive rendering delays.
